$comment: Pre-registration of the code-awareness context-ROI measurement (#579, epic #572; C-089, C-090, C-091..C-094). Registered BEFORE the first measured run, which is the whole point: the pre-build counter-review of 2026-09-17 found that #579 asked for a no-graph control arm but named neither a minimum sample nor a success threshold, and a control arm without a threshold fixed in advance is not evidence — it is a number to argue about afterwards. Amending anything after a run has started invalidates that run: bump registration_version and say which version a report belongs to.
registered_by: Claude Opus 5, for review by Daniel Nevoigt
$comment_status: structure_registered -> numbers_registered. The STRUCTURE below (metric, arms, guards, reporting duties) is fixed. The NUMBERS in `thresholds` are proposals from the counter-review and are NOT yet product-owner decisions: threshold height is Daniel's call, not the implementer's. No measured run may be reported as passing or failing until this file reaches numbers_registered.
question: Does code awareness reduce the context an agent spends before it reaches the right location, without costing latency?
$comment_question: Deliberately one question. #579 also lists secondary observations, and those are reported, but a measurement with several co-equal primary metrics has no honest pass/fail.

primary_metric.name: search_tokens_to_location
primary_metric.definition: Tokens spent on Grep/Glob/Read rounds from the start of a scenario until the agent opens the file:line the scenario names as correct.
primary_metric.$comment: Counted from the same context-ROI telemetry that already charges memory hints (16.3), extended to code. Tokens, not rounds: a single Read of a 2000-line file and five greps cost very different amounts of context and the rounds count hides that. Rounds are reported as a secondary.

secondary_metrics.name: find_code_empty_rate
secondary_metrics.$comment: An honest empty result (4.4 no_answer) is a feature, not a failure — but a tool that is empty most of the time is not earning its place either. Reported so the ratio is visible rather than argued.

secondary_metrics.name: dependents_block_followed_by_edit
secondary_metrics.$comment: How often the Write/Edit block was followed by an edit to a file it listed. This is the only signal that the block was USED rather than merely tolerated.

treatment.name: code awareness on
treatment.description: find_code available and the PreToolUse Write/Edit dependents block active, against a graph built by the pinned Graphify version.

control.name: no-graph control arm
control.description: The same scenarios with code awareness off: no find_code, no dependents block, no graph.
control.$comment: Required by 13.1 and by C-090. A gain measured without the control arm does not count as evidence that the graph caused it — agents get better at a repository simply by working in it, and a single-arm number cannot tell that apart from the feature.

design.paired_on: the same scenario run through both arms
design.$comment_paired: Pairing lowers the required N substantially, and scenario difficulty varies far more than the effect being looked for.
design.$comment_assignment: Which arm runs first per scenario is fixed by the scenario seed before the run, not chosen at run time.

sample.$comment_min: Proposed by the counter-review. Below numbers_registered this is a floor for planning, not a satisfied power calculation: the spread of the primary metric is unknown until a first baseline exists, exactly as the cue experiment registered its structure first and its numbers after the M0 baseline. If the observed spread makes 30 underpowered, the run reports `underpowered` (18.1) rather than a pass.

thresholds.$comment: PROPOSALS, pending product-owner sign-off. Nothing here may be used to declare a pass until status is numbers_registered.
thresholds.$comment_primary: A >= 25 % reduction in search tokens against the control arm, and the difference must hold across scenarios rather than rest on a few outliers — reported with the per-scenario distribution, not as a single mean.

latency_non_regression.$comment: Gating on purpose: a context win bought with latency is not a win. The lane runs at p50 49 ms / p90 87 ms today against a 200 ms target (packages/daemon/src/hook-budgets.ts). The cold-start rule from C-092 means the block is skipped rather than waited for, so a p90 regression here would indicate the warm path is doing more than it claims.

$comment_failure: If the threshold is missed, that is the finding and it is recorded as such. The threshold is not moved after seeing results, and the feature is not quietly re-scoped to match the number it happened to produce. C-090 makes shipped code awareness a mandatory V2.0 criterion WITH substantiated savings — so a miss is a release question, not a reporting question.

run_conditions.$comment_commit: Filled in when the scenario set is checked in. Both arms run against the same frozen commit; a moving tree makes the arms incomparable.
run_conditions.$comment_graphify: The pin from #573. Ten releases went out in twelve days, so an unpinned run measures a moving target.
run_conditions.$comment_build: Per C-091. `graphify update` is inadmissible: it has no --code-only flag and pulls documents into the graph, which would put document content into a measurement about code.

graphify_benchmark_7_3x.$comment: Graphify reports 7.3x fewer tokens in its own benchmark. Per 24 and C-029, no external target value is a Bastra gate. It is not a comparison either: different harness, different reader, different budget.

reporting_duties: The primary metric with its per-scenario distribution, both arms.
The latency comparison against the control arm, with p50 and p90.
Every secondary metric listed above, marked as non-gating.
The registration_version this report belongs to.
An honest status (`underpowered` / `not_evaluable` per 18.1) where the sample does not support a verdict.

deliverables.$comment_scenarios: Not yet written. N >= 30 per arm, each naming the file:line that counts as the correct location.
